stops.name: Oxford, Max Müller and the East that answers back
stops.campa: From his chair at Oxford, the great Sanskritist Max Müller, master of the fifty volumes of the Sacred Books of the East, turns his authority against her. There is no esoteric Buddhism, he declares, no hidden doctrine behind the Shastras that could bear her Theosophy; her secret wisdom is folly and, worse, fraud, no sweet odour in the nostrils of true scholars. The academic East she claimed as her authority rises up to disown her. Yet the books she wrote outsell his; the Masters she carried out of Shigatse have already gone where his footnotes cannot follow, into the living faith of the coming age.
stops.quote: Esoteric Buddhism has no sweet odour in the nostrils of Sanskrit and Pali scholars.

stops.name: Berlin, Steiner turns the stream to the West
stops.campa: Eleven years after her death, a young Austrian scholar, Rudolf Steiner, is made head of the German Section of her Society and reads her root-races and her hidden Masters with new eyes. He grows the German branch to thousands, but he wants a Western, Christian esoteric path, and he will not bow to the Eastern turn or the crowning of a boy as the World Teacher. In 1912 he breaks away to found Anthroposophy, carrying half her German disciples with him. The stream she poured out of Tibet splits at Steiner into an Eastern and a Western river, and both run on into the new century.

stops.name: Adyar, the ashes return; the link held
stops.campa: On the banks of the Adyar river a portion of her ashes comes home, and each May the Society she founded keeps White Lotus Day, reading from the Gita and the Voice of the Silence over the water. Annie Besant, president now, holds the movement she was given; Olcott is long buried in the same soil; the headquarters she chose still stands among the banyans. The link she charged them to keep is not broken. From a burning font at Yekaterinoslav to a river in Madras, the wanderer's ashes complete the last leg of the journey, and the Masters' seat in the world holds its ground.

stops.name: The esoteric descent, Savitri Devi and Miguel Serrano
stops.campa: Far down her lineage, where the light she carried is bent into a darkness she never meant, her root-races and her lost Aryan ages are taken up by others. In India, Savitri Devi weds Hindu cosmology to the myth of the master race and hails a fallen dictator as an avatar of the cycles; in Chile, the diplomat Miguel Serrano builds an esoteric Hitlerism of Thulean gods and cosmic war. They are the shadow-heirs of the Secret Doctrine, reading its cyclical ages into a creed of hatred. The atlas records the descent as it records the ascent: the same seed, in poisoned ground, bearing bitter fruit.
